prompt.context_jp: 夕暮れの光がベランダから差し込み、いつものメイの部屋を柔らかく染めていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 夕暮れの光（　）ベランダから差し込み、いつものメイの部屋を柔らかく染めていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces the evening light as new scene-setting information.

feedback.correct_en: The opening sentence introduces the evening light as a new, visible element of the scene. が marks this fresh, descriptive subject.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat the light as an already-known topic, which doesn't fit a scene-opening description. を is for direct objects.

contrast_examples.en: A wind is blowing. (describing the scene)
The wind is cold. (commenting on a known topic)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサがメイに異動を告げる場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私（　）ここに来られるのは 今日で最後です」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that identifies 'I (coming here)' as the specific referent of 'last day'.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the relative clause 「私がここに来られる」, が marks the subject of the embedded verb. は cannot appear inside a modifying clause like this.
feedback.incorrect_en: は works at the main-clause topic level, not inside a relative clause modifying こと/の.

contrast_examples.en: the food I made (が inside modifying clause)
I made food. (は as main-clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサがいなくなったら…
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ナギサさんがいなくなったら この部屋（　）どうなるんですか」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets 'this room' as the topic being asked about.

feedback.correct_en: The room is the topic of concern Mei is asking about — 'As for this room, what will become of it?' は frames the topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce the room as new information, but here Mei is framing a known thing (her room) as the topic.

contrast_examples.jp: この部屋はどうなるの？
contrast_examples.en: What will happen to this room? (topic framing)
Which room is spacious? (が for identification)

prompt.context_jp: メイの告白に近い場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ナギサさん（　）いない生活なんて 考えられない」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle inside this relative clause modifying 生活.

feedback.correct_en: 「ナギサさんがいない」 modifies 生活. Inside a relative clause, the subject takes が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would break the modifying-clause structure. You cannot say ナギサさんはいない生活.

contrast_examples.en: a day when it rains (が in modifier)
I dislike rain. (は as main topic)

prompt.context_jp: 二人の沈黙の場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 部屋の時計の秒針だけ（　）、二人の沈黙を刻んでいく。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that goes with だけ here to exhaustively identify what breaks the silence.

feedback.correct_en: 'Only the second hand' is being singled out as the unique subject acting in the silent room — exhaustive-listing が works with だけ.
feedback.incorrect_en: だけは is possible but shifts to contrast/topic ('as for only...'); here the narration identifies the single actor, so が fits better.

prompt.context_jp: そんなふうに思える人…
prompt.prompt_jp: 「そんなふうに思える人 ナギサさん（　）いません」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that singles out Nagisa as the only such person.

feedback.correct_en: しかいません ('there is none but ~') exhaustively identifies Nagisa as the sole person who makes her feel that way.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just topicalize Nagisa; が would introduce him but doesn't convey the 'only him' meaning this line carries.

prompt.context_jp: メイの告白への反応。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサ（　）何も答えず、ただ静かにメイを見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets Nagisa as the topic of this narrative sentence.

feedback.correct_en: Nagisa is already an established character in the discourse. The narration shifts the topic back to him with は to describe what he did (or didn't do).
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark him as new/identifying information, but the reader already knows Nagisa; this is a topic-continuation sentence.

prompt.context_jp: おじさんと、と自らを卑下するナギサに対して…
prompt.prompt_jp: メイは黙って首を横に振ったが、その先の言葉（　）すぐに続かない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets up a contrast: she shook her head, BUT the words didn't follow.

feedback.correct_en: Here が introduces 'the words that followed' as a new element in the sentence — they are being newly described (as not coming). は is less natural because this isn't topicalizing previously-known 'next words.'
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply 'as for the next words,' which sounds like contrast with other words; the narrator is simply introducing that her words didn't follow.

contrast_examples.jp: 次の言葉が出なかった。
contrast_examples.en: The next words wouldn't come out. (new info)
Those words are her true feelings. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: 家政夫と夫の違いを考えるメイ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 家事を任せる相手として迎えるのと、夫として迎え入れるのとでは、まったく意味（　）違う。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking 'meaning' as the newly-asserted differing element.

feedback.correct_en: 意味が違う is the standard pattern: が marks what differs. The two situations are the topic (〜では), and 意味 is the new subject being compared.
feedback.incorrect_en: 意味は違う is grammatical but puts contrastive weight on 意味 itself; the natural reading here is 'the meaning is different,' using が.

contrast_examples.jp: 値段は違うが、味は同じ。
contrast_examples.en: The price differs, but the taste is the same. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサが去った理由を考える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 理由（　）もっと単純で、しかも自分の側にある。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'the reason' as the topic the sentence is about.

feedback.correct_en: 'The reason' is already referenced in context; は topicalizes it to then explain what the reason actually is.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce 'reason' as brand-new identification, which doesn't fit — the reason has been looming over this whole passage.

contrast_examples.en: I figured out the reason. (new info)

prompt.context_jp: 元夫がナギサに迫る場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「相原さんには あなた（　）必要なんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that exhaustively identifies Nagisa as the one Aihara needs.

feedback.correct_en: 'It is YOU that Aihara needs' — exhaustive-listing が singles out Nagisa as the unique necessary person.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたは necessary would weaken the force to mere topic comment; the dramatic point is that only he will do.

prompt.context_jp: 告白のあとのナギサの声について。
prompt.prompt_jp: ナギサの声（　）、いつもの家政夫の敬語のままだった。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that topicalizes 'Nagisa's voice' for description.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is describing a known entity (Nagisa's voice) as the topic — 'as for his voice, it was still polite as ever.' は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the voice as newly identified information, but it's an ongoing description of a familiar character.

prompt.context_jp: 敬語のままでも…
prompt.prompt_jp: それでも、その敬語の奥に確かな熱（　）こもっている。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the newly-pointed-out element 'heat' inside the formal speech.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator is newly pointing out 'warmth exists' inside his polite tone. が introduces this fresh observation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would suggest contrast with other things, but here we're introducing the existence of heat as new information.

contrast_examples.en: Tears well up in the eyes. (new state)

prompt.context_jp: ナギサは家事について話す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「何より 私（　）家事（　）好きですから」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle pair for 'I (topic) + housework (object of liking).'

feedback.correct_en: With 好き, the experiencer takes は (topic) and the thing liked takes が. 私は家事が好き is the standard pattern.
feedback.incorrect_en: 好き is an adjective-like predicate; its target takes が, not を. And the experiencer is the topic, so 私は.

contrast_examples.en: As for dogs, it's me that likes them. (odd/contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 二人だけの結婚の形を…
prompt.prompt_jp: 2人だけの結婚の形（　）作っていくのだと思う。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks '2人だけの結婚の形' as the direct object of 作る.

feedback.correct_en: 作る takes a direct object marked by を — 'build/create our own kind of marriage.'
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark it as a subject, which doesn't fit 'build.' は would topicalize it, breaking the sentence rhythm after 歩み寄って.

prompt.context_jp: メイがナギサに伝えた強い気持ち。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私はナギサさんを （　）たくないんです」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that captures 'I don't want to let you go.'

feedback.correct_en: 手放す ('release from one's hand, let go of') is the chapter's key emotional verb — Mei literally doesn't want to release Nagisa from her life.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見逃す means 'overlook/let slip by,' and 手伝う means 'help' — neither matches 'don't want to let go of a person.'

contrast_examples.jp: この機会を手放したくない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't want to let this chance go.
Don't let go of my hand.

prompt.context_jp: メイのプロポーズ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「じゃあ 私たち… （　）ませんか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for a proposal of marriage.

feedback.correct_en: 結婚しませんか is a standard proposal 'Won't you marry me?' Mei is literally proposing here.
feedback.incorrect_en: 相談 means 'consult' and 契約 means 'contract' — too businesslike, and not what she's asking.

prompt.context_jp: メイの自己反省。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「私が ちゃんと話し合うことから （　）から 3日でクーリング･オフか…」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'ran away / avoided.'

feedback.correct_en: 〜から逃げる ('to run from / avoid') fits Mei's self-blame about dodging the serious discussion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 降りる ('get off') and 抜く ('pull out') don't form idiomatic phrases with 話し合うことから.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサがメイに感謝を伝える。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あなたは いつも そうやって 私の肩の荷を （　）しまいますね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that completes 'take the load off my shoulders.'

feedback.correct_en: 肩の荷を下ろす is a set phrase meaning 'to be relieved of a burden.' Nagisa is saying Mei always lifts his worries away.
feedback.incorrect_en: 肩の荷を持つ/上げる aren't idiomatic — the fixed phrase requires 下ろす.

contrast_examples.en: A weight is off my shoulders.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサは反対しそうだと感じるメイ。
prompt.prompt_jp: このまま押し通そうとしても、ナギサは首を（　）振ってくれない気がする。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the direction word completing 'won't nod yes.'

feedback.correct_en: 首を縦に振る = 'nod (agree).' Mei fears Nagisa won't give his assent.
feedback.incorrect_en: 首を横に振る means the opposite — 'shake the head (refuse).' 上に doesn't form an idiom.

prompt.context_jp: トライアル結婚を提案する直前。
prompt.prompt_jp: 口にしてしまえば、もう後には（　）ない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb for 'can't turn back / can't retract.'

feedback.correct_en: 後には引けない is a set phrase meaning 'there's no turning back / can't back down.'
feedback.incorrect_en: 見える and 返す don't form this idiom.

contrast_examples.en: I can't go back at this point.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサが突然いなくなった朝。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「たった3日で 私 愛想を（　）された？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb that forms 'got given up on / lost patience with me.'

feedback.correct_en: 愛想を尽かす = 'to lose patience / give up on someone.' Passive 尽かされる means 'to be given up on.'
feedback.incorrect_en: The idiom is fixed — only 尽かす completes 愛想を〜. The other verbs don't collocate.

contrast_examples.en: to be given up on by someone.

prompt.context_jp: メイが反省を語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「（　）てました 私も変わっていかないと ダメですね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the verb meaning 'relied too much / was spoiled.'

feedback.correct_en: 甘える ('to presume on someone's kindness') captures Mei's admission that she was depending on Nagisa too much.
feedback.incorrect_en: 任せる means 'entrust (a task),' and 頼る means 'rely on' — both close but 甘えてました is the natural self-reflective phrase here.

contrast_examples.en: Sorry for taking advantage of your kindness.

prompt.context_jp: メイが自分の気持ちに気づく瞬間。
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as Mei's emotional confession?

choices.text: ナギサさんがいない生活なんて 考えられない
ナギサさんはいない生活なんて 考えられない

feedback.correct_en: Inside a noun-modifying clause (〜がいない生活), the subject takes が. は cannot appear in that position.
feedback.incorrect_en: ナギサさんはいない生活 is ungrammatical — は doesn't work inside a relative clause modifying 生活.

contrast_examples.en: a house where father is absent
Father is always at home. (main clause)

prompt.context_jp: メイが想像する、夫となったナギサの朝の声。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line matches the 'casual husband' tone the chapter explicitly contrasts with Nagisa's usual 敬語?

choices.text: おはよう 時間だよ メイ
おはようございます メイさん お時間です

feedback.correct_en: The chapter notes 敬語のない、砕けた口ぶり — a casual tone without honorifics. 'おはよう' and 'メイ' (no さん) capture that shift.
feedback.incorrect_en: The polite version is how the real Nagisa actually speaks; in the imagined-husband fantasy, he drops keigo entirely.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサがメイに返す言葉。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line best mirrors Mei's earlier 手放したくない confession as Nagisa's reply?

choices.text: 私も あなたを 手放したくないんです
私も あなたが 手放したくないんです

feedback.correct_en: 手放す is a transitive verb; its object takes を. The echo of Mei's line uses あなたを 手放したくない.
feedback.incorrect_en: あなたが 手放したくない would ungrammatically make 'you' the subject of the wanting-to-release.

prompt.context_jp: ナギサがいつも台所に立っているはずだった、という描写。
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds more natural as narration explaining a habitual pattern that's now broken?

choices.text: ナギサはいつも、彼女が起きる前から台所に立っているはずだった。
ナギサがいつも、彼女は起きる前から台所に立っているはずだった。

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes Nagisa the known topic (は) and uses が inside the subordinate clause 彼女が起きる前. This matches Japanese discourse conventions.
feedback.incorrect_en: Swapping particles turns Nagisa into new information and breaks the subordinate clause subject-marking, sounding unnatural.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は私が帰る前に寝る。
contrast_examples.en: Dad goes to bed before I get home. (natural は/が split)

contrast_examples.jp: 父が私は帰る前に寝る。

prompt.context_jp: メイがナギサと一緒にいる時の気持ち。
prompt.prompt_en: Which expression is more natural for 'I feel genuinely at ease'?

choices.text: 心から安心するんです

feedback.correct_en: 心から is the set adverbial 'from the heart / genuinely.' It collocates naturally with emotional verbs like 安心する.
feedback.incorrect_en: 心で安心する doesn't form a standard collocation — Japanese uses 心から for this nuance.
